differentiator: The plan lives on disk as plain markdown, so a context wipe or crash can't erase it -- the agent reads the file back and picks up exactly where it left off.

concepts.name: STILL THERE (picked)
concepts.world: A warm amber-phosphor field, like a log or a ledger left glowing on a screen at night. Everything is written down, and the writing outlasts the machine.
concepts.shows: A plan appears as a file object. Three real markdown files (task_plan.md, findings.md, progress.md) run with live status. Hooks re-read the plan before each move. Then /clear hits and the frame whites out. The plan re-materializes from disk intact and the work resumes. It closes back on the file object, rhyming the open.
concepts.money_shot: The restore: a hard wipe blanks the frame, then the morph reconstitutes the plan and the eyebrow reads 'reads the file back'. The one thing only this project does, dead center.
concepts.why_creator_reposts: It dramatizes his actual thesis (markdown is the agent's working memory on disk) as a feeling, not a diagram. It flatters the engineering, not the star chart.
concepts.why_stranger_stops: The wipe is a pattern interrupt. A white-out mid-video, then the thing you thought was gone snaps back. You watch to see how.
concepts.light: Shader amber field lifts every frame; the /clear flash is a full bright white-out (the brightest beat); the 25k count-up is the second bright beat.
concepts.cuts: Hard cuts by default; the reserved bloom fires once on the restore cut; motion carries through (the metaphor network is already converging when its scene enters).

concepts.name: THE LEDGER
concepts.world: An accountant's ledger metaphor: the agent balances its own books, every decision written to a line before it acts.
concepts.shows: Lines of a plan being written and checked off, a completion gate stamping done only when the ledger actually moved.
concepts.money_shot: The gate refusing to stamp 'done' because the ledger didn't progress (the deterministic completion gate).
concepts.why_creator_reposts: Honors the completion-gate engineering. But it is drier and leans on a rules idea that is hard to make visceral in 3 seconds.
concepts.why_stranger_stops: Weaker -- a ledger reads as bookkeeping, not a breakthrough.
concepts.light: Warm, but risks a lot of small mono type (readability gate risk).
concepts.cuts: Would lean terminal-ish, close to the rejected default.

concepts.name: THE HIJACK
concepts.world: A thriller framing around the v3.4.0 bug: a read-only bot sharing a working directory gets its plan hijacked, fake completions written into its files.
concepts.shows: Two agents on one directory, one writing fabricated 'done' into the other's plan, then the PLANNING_DISABLED=1 flag shutting it down.
concepts.money_shot: The opt-out flag killing the hijack.
concepts.why_creator_reposts: It is the surprising_detail and shows real reliability work. But it centers a bug over the core value, which could read as criticism, not tribute.
concepts.why_stranger_stops: Intriguing but needs too much setup to land the stakes in 28s.
concepts.light: Two-pane, workable, but the story is inside-baseball.

wow_bets: The /clear white-out into the morph restore -- a real pattern interrupt, not a slideshow.
The plan object bookends (open and close rhyme) for a clean X autoloop.
Warm amber field against a run of cool-dark videos -- it will look like a different production in the feed.
